data.schema.message.why: Reuse list and read results while server cache hints allow it.
data.schema.message.how: Reads cache scope and TTL hints from results, keyed per peer, with private entries partitioned.

specification.title: Address policy
specification.text: `AuthorizationManager` sends its metadata and token requests through the resolver in `src/transport/auth/metadata_resolver.rs`. A host that discovered metadata may resolve to any public address. A loopback or private address is allowed only when the base URL itself names one (an IP literal or `localhost`). Link-local, cloud metadata, unspecified, broadcast, multicast and reserved addresses are never allowed. The same policy applies to the base host, so it cannot be rebound to an internal address. Configured proxy hosts are not filtered. `enterprise.rs` does not apply this policy itself: it takes any `OAuthHttpClient` the caller passes.

specification.title: Flows
specification.text: The manager discovers protected-resource and authorization-server metadata (a cross-origin `resource_metadata` URL is allowed), registers a client when needed, runs the authorization code flow with PKCE `S256`, refreshes with only the granted scopes, and can upgrade scopes. With `auth-client-credentials-jwt` it also supports the client-credentials flow with a signed JWT assertion.

code.store.credential.why: Keep tokens and in-flight PKCE and CSRF state between process runs and across instances.
code.store.credential.how: CredentialStore and StateStore traits with in-memory defaults the caller may replace.

upstream.server.authorization.why: Discover metadata, register the client, obtain and refresh access tokens with PKCE S256 and scope upgrade.
upstream.server.authorization.how: Authorization code flow and client-credentials flow over HTTPS; returns access and refresh tokens.

code.client.oauth.why: Obtain an MCP access token without user interaction from an enterprise ID token or refresh token.
code.client.oauth.how: Exchanges the enterprise credential for an ID-JAG, then redeems it at the MCP authorization server, using an OAuthHttpClient the caller supplies (default_oauth_http_client in auth.rs).

data.schema.message.why: Protect the requestState string a server returns in InputRequiredResult and receives back from an untrusted client.
data.schema.message.how: Seals a payload with HMAC-SHA256 and rejects forged or altered values on open.

specification.title: Server-initiated work
specification.text: `ClientHandler` answers sampling, elicitation and roots requests and receives logging, progress, resource-updated and list-changed notifications. `handler/client/progress.rs` dispatches progress notifications to subscribers by progress token. Elicitation schemas are built with the typed builder in `model/elicitation_schema.rs`.

data.schema.message.why: Receive server-initiated requests (sampling, elicitation, roots listing) and notifications as typed values and return typed results.
data.schema.message.how: Trait with one default method per server request or notification.

specification.title: Method surface
specification.text: `ServerHandler` has one default method for each client request and notification: initialize, ping, tools, prompts, resources, completion, logging, tasks, skills and subscriptions. Each default returns method-not-found, so an author overrides only what the server supports. Calls to `tasks/*` and `skills/*` are refused with `-32601` unless `get_info` declares the matching extension capability. `Router<S>` in `router.rs` combines a `ToolRouter`, a `PromptRouter` and a handler and itself implements `ServerHandler`.

code.router.prompt.why: Dispatch prompts/list and prompts/get to registered prompt functions.
code.router.prompt.how: Router holds a prompt route table and calls the route by prompt name.

code.router.tool.why: Dispatch tools/list and tools/call to registered tool functions.
code.router.tool.how: Router holds a tool route table and calls the route by tool name.

data.schema.message.why: Receive typed request parameters and return typed results for every server-side MCP method.
data.schema.message.how: Trait with one default method per request or notification; defaults return method-not-found.

data.schema.message.why: Route messages to the session that owns a Mcp-Session-Id.
data.schema.message.how: Keeps per-session channels of client and server JSON-RPC messages; local manager is in memory, never manager rejects sessions, EventStore and SessionStore traits allow external persistence and SSE replay.

data.schema.message.why: Report task state and results to tasks/get, tasks/update and tasks/cancel.
data.schema.message.how: Holds DetailedTask records with working, input_required and terminal status, TTL expiry and cooperative cancellation.

upstream.runtime.async.why: Spawn each long operation and time out overdue tasks.
upstream.runtime.async.how: Spawns tasks on tokio with cancellation tokens.

data.schema.message.why: Describe each prompt and return GetPromptResult.
data.schema.message.how: Uses Prompt, PromptMessage and GetPromptResult types.

specification.title: Registration paths
specification.text: A tool enters the `ToolRouter` through the `tool_router` macro, or by implementing `SyncTool` or `AsyncTool` and adding it with `with_tool`. Parameters are extracted with `Parameters<T>` and results are wrapped with `Json<T>`, which also fills `outputSchema`. Extractors in `handler/server/common.rs` (`Extension`, `RequestId`, `ToolCallContext`) let a tool read request context. `tool_name_validation.rs` checks names against the SEP format (1 to 128 characters of letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.`) and only warns.

data.schema.message.why: Describe each tool and wrap its output as a CallToolResult.
data.schema.message.how: Uses Tool, CallToolResult and Content types; checks tool names against the SEP name format and warns when they do not conform.

upstream.generator.json_schema.why: Publish an input schema and an output schema for each tool.
upstream.generator.json_schema.how: Derives schemas from the parameter and Json output types.

upstream.macro.tool.why: Turn annotated methods into registered tool routes without hand-written glue.
upstream.macro.tool.how: The tool_router and tool attribute macros generate the route table and handler calls.

specification.title: Peer and lifecycle
specification.text: `serve_server` and `serve_client` return a `RunningService` that owns the message loop and exposes a `Peer`. `Peer` sends requests with optional timeouts (including reset on progress and a maximum total), sends notifications, and cancels a pending request. Client lifecycle mode selection (`ClientLifecycleMode`) and `negotiate_protocol_version` decide whether an `initialize` handshake runs: protocol `2026-07-28` has none. `src/service/server.rs` adds server-to-client calls: `create_message` (sampling), `elicit` and `elicit_url`, and list-changed notifications with subscription filters.

code.cache.response.why: Serve repeat client calls from cache.
code.cache.response.how: Peer consults the cache before sending list and read requests.

code.handler.client.why: Answer server-initiated requests when this process acts as the client.
code.handler.client.how: Calls the ClientHandler method that matches the request enum variant.

code.handler.server.why: Answer each incoming request when this process acts as the server.
code.handler.server.how: Calls the ServerHandler method that matches the request enum variant.

code.transport.why: Exchange framed messages with the peer.
code.transport.how: Transport trait gives a send and a receive half the service loop drives.

data.schema.message.why: Encode outgoing and decode incoming JSON-RPC requests, results and notifications.
data.schema.message.how: Defines typed request, result and notification enums for each MCP method.

upstream.runtime.async.why: Run the message loop, request timeouts and cancellation as tasks.
upstream.runtime.async.how: Spawns the loop on tokio and uses cancellation tokens.

specification.title: Scope and status
specification.text: `rmcp` 3.9.0 (released 2026-11-05 per `CHANGELOG.md`) is a Rust library for both roles of the Model Context Protocol (MCP). `ProtocolVersion::LATEST` is `2026-07-28`; the code also negotiates `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26` and `2024-11-05`. The crate has no binary. `build.rs` only sets `core.hooksPath` when the crate sits in its original workspace, so it has no effect on the published crate.

specification.title: Material not in this folder
specification.text: The `#[tool]`, `#[tool_router]`, `#[prompt]` and `#[tool_handler]` macros come from the separate crate `rmcp-macros` 3.9.0. This folder does not contain that crate. The README links `../../README.md` and `docs/OAUTH_SUPPORT.md`, which are also not in the published package. The macro behavior is therefore recorded from its use in `src/` documentation, not from its source.

specification.title: Feature gating
specification.text: `default` enables `server`, `macros` and `base64`. Each transport, `auth`, `elicitation`, `request-state` and `client` sit behind a Cargo feature, so a build contains only the elements whose features are on. The `local` feature drops the `Send` bounds and removes `StreamableHttpService`.

code.cache.response.how: Per-peer response cache configured with ClientCacheConfig.

code.client.oauth.why: Let clients authorize against protected MCP servers.
code.client.oauth.how: auth feature adds AuthorizationManager and credential stores.

code.client.oauth.enterprise.why: Let enterprise clients obtain tokens without a user prompt.

code.handler.client.how: ClientHandler trait re-exported at the crate root under the client feature.

code.handler.server.why: Let the server author supply behavior for each MCP method.
code.handler.server.how: ServerHandler trait re-exported at the crate root.

code.manager.task.why: Let servers run long tool calls as pollable tasks.
code.manager.task.how: TaskManager spawns operations and answers tasks/get, update and cancel.

code.runtime.service.why: Serve and call MCP over one connection in either role.
code.runtime.service.how: serve_server and serve_client start the message loop and return a RunningService with a Peer.

code.transport.why: Carry JSON-RPC messages over stdio, child process or Streamable HTTP.
code.transport.how: Transport and IntoTransport traits plus feature-gated implementations.

code.transport.http.client.why: Let a client reach a remote server over Streamable HTTP.
code.transport.http.client.how: Feature transport-streamable-http-client with a reqwest backend option.

code.transport.http.server.why: Let a server be hosted inside an HTTP stack.
code.transport.http.server.how: StreamableHttpService is a tower service mounted in a router.

code.transport.process.child.why: Let a client start and talk to a local server process.

code.transport.stdio.why: Let a server speak MCP over its own stdin and stdout.
code.transport.stdio.how: stdio() returns a ready transport under the transport-io feature.

data.schema.message.why: Share one typed definition of the protocol between both roles.
data.schema.message.how: model module with requests, results, notifications, capabilities, content, tools, prompts, resources, tasks, skills and elicitation schemas.

specification.title: Layout
specification.text: `Cargo.toml` declares 94 `[[test]]` targets, one per file `tests/test_*.rs`; the folder also holds data folders (`test_deserialization`, `test_message_schema`, `test_list_tools_result`) and fixtures in `tests/common`. 30 of the 94 files create an in-memory `tokio::io::duplex` stream between a client and a server. This crate copy has no `tests/test_package_license.rs`, which `Cargo.toml` excludes. The map does not claim that any test passes: no test was run during intake.

code.sdk.mcp.why: Check protocol behavior: lifecycle, cancellation, progress, auth classification, caching, MRTR, tasks, schema stability and version negotiation.
code.sdk.mcp.how: 94 integration files declared as [[test]] targets in Cargo.toml; 30 connect a client to a server over an in-memory duplex stream, using fixtures in tests/common.

upstream.runtime.async.why: Read and write byte streams and spawn background tasks without blocking the caller.
upstream.runtime.async.how: Supplies tokio I/O traits, channels and task spawning.

code.client.oauth.why: Attach a bearer token and recover from 401 and 403 responses.
code.client.oauth.how: AuthClient wraps the HTTP client and adds the access token header.

code.transport.why: Fit the Transport contract as a worker transport.
code.transport.how: Implemented as a Worker run by WorkerTransport.

upstream.server.mcp.why: Post requests and receive responses and server messages over HTTP and server-sent events.
upstream.server.mcp.how: POST with session id and Mcp-* headers, a GET SSE stream with Last-Event-ID reconnect and backoff; optional Unix-socket client and reqwest backend.

code.handler.server.why: Create a handler per session or per stateless request.
code.handler.server.how: Factory closure builds a ServerHandler and runs it with serve_directly or serve_server.

code.manager.session.why: Create, resume and close sessions under legacy protocol versions.
code.manager.session.how: Calls SessionManager to create a session and route each request.

code.runtime.service.why: Run the MCP service loop on each session transport.
code.runtime.service.how: Calls serve_server_with_ct over a worker transport.

upstream.client.mcp.why: Accept POST, GET and DELETE requests and answer with JSON or server-sent events.
upstream.client.mcp.how: Tower service that validates Host, Origin, Accept and Mcp-* headers, caps body size, serves stateless for protocol 2026-07-28 and later.

code.transport.why: Let a client talk to a server it starts as a subprocess.
code.transport.how: Spawns the command, uses its pipes as the byte stream, and sends SIGTERM before killing it on graceful shutdown.

code.transport.why: Be usable wherever a Transport is expected.
code.transport.how: Wraps the process stdin and stdout as an async read and write pair, then uses the generic async read-write transport.

specification.title: Status
specification.text: The websocket transport is not built. `src/transport/ws.rs` holds one comment line: "Maybe we don't really need a ws implementation?". `src/transport.rs` lines 110-111 hold a commented-out `#[cfg(feature = "transport-ws")] pub mod ws;`. `Cargo.toml` defines no `transport-ws` feature.

specification.title: Reason to investigate
specification.text: `src/transport.rs` documents `SinkStreamTransport` as the route for a websocket connection. A websocket transport might therefore be left out on purpose. The evidence does not show whether the file is a stale placeholder or a deferred decision.

code.sdk.mcp.why: Expose tools, resources and prompts to AI assistants without hand-writing the protocol.
code.sdk.mcp.how: Provides a ServerHandler trait, tool routing and server transports that answer MCP requests.

specification.name: Specification
specification.description: Prose that the skeleton leaves out on purpose: what each element does, how it behaves and why, as blocks with Markdown heading levels.
specification.instruction:
Write each block in TASTE: Technically Accurate, Simple, Transparent English. A block adds what the map leaves out on purpose; do not repeat what the element's fields and wants already say.
- Start with what the element does or holds. Then give the detail that explains it.
- Name the element, field or command instead of starting with "it", "this" or "they". A block is often read alone.
- Use the project's terms and exact identifiers. Use one term for one thing. Put identifiers in backticks.
- Write one claim per sentence. Aim for 25 words or fewer per sentence and six sentences or fewer per paragraph. Never cut a condition, an exception or a reason to meet a length target.
- Use lowercase must, should, may, can and might with their TASTE meanings. Do not write SHALL or capitalized MUST.
- Say whether something is built, proposed or planned. Do not describe planned behavior as if it exists.
- Replace words such as simple, robust or fast with the behavior or a measurement.
- Define an abbreviation at its first use. Keep noun clusters to three nouns.
- Leave out openings such as "This section describes", repeated points, analogies and promotion.
- Prefer start, use, adjust, perform and end over kick off/launch/begin, utilize/leverage, modify/change/alter, execute/run and terminate/stop/abort, when the meaning stays the same.
- Do not put Markdown heading lines in the text. Set the block's level and title instead.
